`fix` (`api`): **Apply settings patch validation and stop per-item json patch loss**:

Per-item JSON Patch operations on settings lists mutated the list
instance returned by the property getter in place, so property setters
never ran and the changes were silently discarded or left derived state
stale.

- Made `TMDBSettings.InternalImageLanguageOrder` the single source of
  truth with a normalizing setter and turned the enum `ImageLanguageOrder`
  into a computed `[JsonIgnore]` view, so per-item ops on
  `/TMDB/ImageLanguageOrder` mutate the stored list
- Added `ImportSettings.ResetExcludeRegexes` and invalidate the compiled
  exclude regex cache in `SettingsProvider.OnSettingsSaved`, since
  per-item ops on `/Import/Exclude` bypass the cache-invalidating setter
- Returned 400 via `ValidationProblem` from `SettingsController.SetSettings`
  when `ApplyTo` errors leave `ModelState` invalid instead of saving and
  returning 200
- Added regression tests covering per-item ops on both lists, whole-array
  replace normalization, and ModelState error surfacing
`fix` (`database`): **Guard the 182 primary-key alters against dropped tables**.

`fix`: **Collect a shoko season's TMDB seasons from its own episodes**:

`IShokoSeason.TmdbSeasons` and `IShokoSeason.LinkedSeasons` on `AnimeSeason`
filtered the series' episodes with `SeasonNumber != seasonNumber`. An episode's
season number follows its type, so the filter never matched and both always came
back empty. They now match the season's own episodes, like the rest of the type.

- Added `AnimeSeasonTmdbLinkTests` covering a normal and a specials season

`fix` (`api`): **Serve the HLS manifest from its session path**:

`Stream/Hls/master.m3u8` returned a manifest whose `init.mp4` and
`segment-{index}.m4s` URIs resolved against `Stream/Hls/`, where no route
exists, so no HLS transform could be played. It now mints the session and
redirects to `Stream/Hls/{sessionID}/master.m3u8`, and `BuildManifest`
carries the request's query string onto every URI so an `apikey` in the
query reaches the segments too. `Stream/Direct` keeps the query string
across its redirect for the same reason.

`feat` (`abstractions`): **Add `IHlsPresentationRendition`**:

Added an HLS rendition shape that serves its own presentation, for output
the core's single-variant, fixed-duration manifest cannot describe:
alternate audio renditions, a bitrate ladder, or segments cut at source
keyframes.

- `OpenResourceAsync` receives every request under
  `Stream/Hls/{sessionID}/`, including `master.m3u8`, with the relative
  path and the query string
- `HlsResource` carries the content type, an optional `ETag`, and the
  position observers are notified with
- `IHlsStreamRendition` and its routes are unchanged

`fix` (`api`): **Mark optional authentication on the stream pipeline routes**:

The `Stream/Transforms`, `Stream/Hls` and `Stream/Direct` routes let
anonymous callers through only when `AllowAnonymousFileStreamingInAPIv3`
is set, like `Stream` itself, but were missing `OptionalAuthentication`,
so the OpenAPI document did not list the API key for them.

`fix` (`streaming`): **Keep a stream session alive while a response is streaming**:

A session's idle time only reset when a request arrived, so a progressive
stream played over one long range request looked idle and was evicted,
with its rendition disposed, under the open response. Streams served from
a session are now wrapped by `StreamSession.Track`, and
`EvictExpiredSessions` skips a session until they are all disposed.
`SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes` now defaults to 10 instead of 3, so a paused
HLS player that has stopped requesting segments survives a longer pause.

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Serve rendition resources for either delivery mode**:

Split the resource half of `IHlsPresentationRendition` into
`IStreamRenditionResources`, which any rendition can implement to serve
files beside its stream, such as subtitle tracks and fonts.

- Renamed `HlsResource` and `HlsResourceRequest` to `StreamResource` and
  `StreamResourceRequest`
- `IHlsPresentationRendition` is now `IStreamRenditionResources` with
  `master.m3u8` as its entry point
- Added `Stream/Direct/{sessionID}/{**path}`, and `Stream/Hls/{sessionID}/{**path}`
  now serves any rendition that implements the interface

`feat` (`api`): **Describe stream sessions**:

Added `IStreamRenditionResources.DescribeAsync`, so a rendition can tell
clients what it offers beyond the stream, and `Stream/Sessions/{sessionID}`
to serve it.

- `StreamDescription` lists video and audio tracks (ordinal, codec,
  language, dimensions or channels, default, per-user rank), subtitles,
  attachments, chapters and extras, plus rendition-specific `Metadata`
- The endpoint resolves every resource path to a URL carrying the
  request's query string, and reports the session's transform and
  delivery mode
- The stream redirects, the session manifest and the progressive stream
  now send `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` pointing at it

`feat` (`streaming`): **Resume evicted stream sessions under the same id**:

A client returning to a session after it was evicted, such as a player
resumed after a long pause, got a 404 and playback stopped. Sessions
started through `Stream/Hls/master.m3u8` or `Stream/Direct` now record
their video, transform and query string, and a request naming an evicted
session within `EvictedSessionResumeHours` (default 24) rebuilds the
rendition under the same id, once per session however many requests
arrive together. The session's cache directory is no longer named after
its id, so a rebuild cannot race the deletion of the old one.

`fix` (`import`): **Fall back to the episode watched record when transferring state**:

SetWatchedStateIfNeeded only copied watched state from still-existing
sibling files, so replacing a watched release (e.g. TV with blu-ray)
after the watched copy was deleted left the new file unwatched, even
though the episode-level record still carried the state.

- Add an episode-level AnimeEpisode_User fallback (newest watched date
  and playback count) under UseExistingFileWatchedStatus
- Skip users whose new file is already watched to avoid overwrites

`fix` (`anidb`): **Read `code` attribute from `<error>` in mylist response** ([#1440](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1440)):

AniDB's error element uses `code`, not `value`. The wrong attribute
name made `Attribute("code")!` throw `ArgumentNullException` on any
error response (e.g. `<error code="310">illegal input or access
denied</error>`), masking the real error and crashing MyList refresh.

`fix` (`db`): **Tolerate quoted identifiers when patching stored SQLite DDL**:

A tool that rebuilt a table outside Shoko, such as DB Browser for SQLite,
stores the CREATE TABLE with every identifier double-quoted in
`sqlite_master`. Migrations that tighten a column's nullability or retype
it patch the stored blueprint in place, and the patch regexes could not
see past the quoting, so migration `164.1` aborted on such a database
with `Could not find a definition for Title` and left it blocked.

- Accept an optional `"` pair around the column name in
  `NotNullVariantOf` and `RetypedVariantOf`, keeping the quotes in the
  rebuilt DDL
- Pin the affected user's exact table shape in regression tests for both
  paths

`misc`: **Bump abstractions**.

`fix` (`anilist`): **Decompress responses from the `Anilist` http client**:

The `Anilist` client advertised gzip, deflate and brotli via
`Accept-Encoding` but had no handler with `AutomaticDecompression`, so
brotli-encoded GraphQL responses were handed to `JsonNode.Parse` still
compressed and failed with "'0x1B' is an invalid start of a value".
Gave it the same `SocketsHttpHandler` setup as the `Default` client.

`fix` (`relocation`): **Resolve the managed folder path before containment checks**:

The containment check compared a fully-resolved path against the raw
folder path, which never matches on Windows where GetFullPath adds a
drive letter. Resolve the folder path once and use it for the
comparison and downstream relative-path math. The source-location test
asserts against the folder's platform-normalized path so it holds on
both platforms.

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Expose `IAuthenticationThrottleService` to plugins and back it by settings**:

Exposed the authentication throttling to plugins through `IAuthenticationThrottleService`, so plugins that authenticate users, such as Forgotten for its password reset and username recovery flows, share the core's lockouts instead of keeping their own. Moved its policy from constants into server settings.

- Added `IAuthenticationThrottleService` to the abstractions. It accepts only an `HttpContext`, a `HubCallerContext` or an `IUser`, so plugins can't lock out or reset arbitrary keys
- Added `ThrottleAuthentication` to the interface. It checks a username that need not exist, so unknown and existing usernames get the same answer
- Renamed `LoginThrottler` to `AuthenticationThrottleService` and moved it to `Shoko.Server.Services`
- Kept the raw username overloads `internal` for `UserService`, and prefixed username keys with `user:` so they can't collide with `ip:` client keys
- Added `AuthenticationThrottleSettings` under `Web.AuthenticationThrottle`, with ranges enforced by the settings validation and a check that the initial lockout doesn't exceed the max lockout
- Cached the policy in `AuthenticationThrottleService` and refreshed it when the settings are saved; lowering the max lockout also shortens existing lockouts
- Switched the login controllers to `IAuthenticationThrottleService` and removed the `LoginThrottlerExtensions` helpers

`feat` (`api`): **Mark optional authentication in the OpenAPI document**:

Added `OptionalAuthenticationAttribute` for endpoints that accept authentication but don't always require it, and made `AuthorizeOperationFilter` list the API key as optional for them.

- Emitted an empty security requirement next to the API key for marked endpoints that don't require authorization, including endpoints without any authorization attributes
- Marked `/api/v3/Init/Status`, whose response adds details for authenticated callers
- Marked the `/api/v3/File/{fileID}/Stream*` endpoints, which only let anonymous callers through when `AllowAnonymousFileStreamingInAPIv3` is enabled, so Swagger UI now sends the key to them

`feat` (`api`): **Document the `apikey` query parameter in the OpenAPI document**:

Added an `ApiKeyQuery` security scheme for the `apikey` query parameter, which the authentication handler already accepted but the OpenAPI document never described.

- Listed the header and query parameter schemes as alternative requirements wherever the API key is required or optional
- Moved the scheme names into constants on `AuthorizeOperationFilter`, kept the existing `ApiKey` name for the header scheme

`feat` (`abstractions`): **Add features for plugins to advertise to clients**:

Added `IPlugin.GetFeatures` so plugins can advertise what they add to the server, e.g. Forgotten advertising password reset so a login page knows to offer it.

- Added `PluginFeature` with a lowercase kebab-case name, a `Version` defaulting to `1.0.0`, a `PluginFeatureVisibility` defaulting to `Authenticated`, and optional `JObject` metadata
- Added `PluginFeature.IsValid`, which rejects names that aren't kebab-case or exceed `MaxNameLength`, missing versions, and undefined visibilities
- Added `LocalPluginInfo.GetFeatures`, which drops invalid and duplicate features instead of correcting them, trims versions to major, minor, and patch, and keeps the order the plugin returned

`feat` (`api`): **Add `/api/v3/Plugin/Features` endpoint**:

Added an endpoint for clients to discover the features advertised by the active plugins, before or after signing in.

- Returned only anonymous features to unauthenticated callers, also authenticated features to users, and every feature to administrators
- Included the plugin ID on every feature, and the full plugin info only for administrators, so anonymous callers can't fingerprint installed plugin versions
- Ordered features by plugin load order, then in the order each plugin advertised them
- Logged each dropped feature once per run, and skipped the features of a plugin that threw instead of failing the whole response

`feat` (`auth`): **Add password-reset file on startup and harden API login**:

Add a startup password recovery path: a password-reset.json file in the

credentials. The file is kept when the user is not found so it can be

`fix` (`abstractions`): **Make `LanguageExtensions` unknown-language tracking thread-safe** ([#1426](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1426)):

`GetTitleLanguage()` mutated an unsynchronized static `HashSet<string>`
to dedupe unknown-language reports. Concurrent callers (e.g. API
requests building File DTOs) corrupted it and crashed with
`InvalidOperationException`.

Replaced the `HashSet` with a `ConcurrentDictionary` used as a set, so
no external synchronization is needed at any call site.

`fix` (`db`): **Declare the AniList text columns as utf8mb4 on MySQL**:

The schema parity job failed on 26 AniList text columns that MySQL
reported as nullable while SQLite and SQL Server had them `NOT NULL`.
The tables declared their text columns with the old `UTF8` character
set, so the after-patch charset fix rebuilt every one of them with a
bare `MODIFY`, which drops anything left unstated, the null constraint
included. Declared them `utf8mb4` with the unicode collation up front,
matching the repaired columns from v185, so the fix leaves them alone.

Verified with `scripts/compare_schemas.sh` against MariaDB and SQL
Server: all twelve parity tests pass.

`fix`: **Count missing TMDB episode links against the AniDB episode id**:

`FilterableAnimeSeries.MissingTmdbEpisodeLinks` and the group
counterpart collected the linked AniDB episode ids and then looked up
each episode's Shoko id in that set, so the count was wrong whenever the
two id spaces diverged. Compared against `AniDB_EpisodeID`, and left out

`fix` (`abstractions`): **Make the missing TMDB episode links selector read its own count**:

`MissingTmdbEpisodeLinksSelector` returned `MissingEpisodes`, the count

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Log the AniDB anime title instead of the title object**:

`AniDB_Anime.PreferredTitle` is the `ITitle` object, so the episode

the anime title should have been. Switched them to `AniDB_Anime.Title`.

`fix` (`api`): **Route the TMDB episode cross-references by episode id**:

`GET /api/v3/Episode/{episodeID}/TMDB/Episode/CrossReferences` declared

`refactor` (`tmdb`): **Share the air-date scoring helpers with other providers**:

Moved `CalculateAirDateProbability`, `CalculateAirDateDistance` and the

`feat` (`anilist`): **Add the anilist metadata provider**:

Ported the AniList integration shelved in April onto the current
image manager and queue, and finished the parts the original left
unimplemented.

- Metadata service with quick and full refresh, entity locks, a
  sliding-window rate limiter that follows AniList's quota headers,
  pauses the AniList jobs on 429 and 5xx responses, and traces every
  call like the TMDB client does
- Episodes synthesised from the airing schedule, with the schedule id
  stored separately and the air time kept in UTC; episode ids are
  packed as `(animeId << 12) | episodeNumber`
- Linking service mirroring `TmdbLinkingService`, with the new
  `DateAndNumberMatches` and `DateOffsetMatches` ratings; episode
  numbers only ever corroborate a date match
- Tags, studios, relations, characters, staff, images, external links
  and the trailer, all exposed as resources and through the
  abstractions; the main title is typed by its transcription language
  and the preferred title follows the title language order
- APIv3 controller with the TMDB-shaped include model, search,
  refresh with quick mode, series-level linking, image download,
  export and import with comments, plus the filter expressions and
  selectors
- Database tables for the three backends, settings, actions, recurring
  purge, and the WebUI-facing 502/503 handling for upstream failures

`fix` (`abstractions`): **Add Faroese, Twi, Chamorro and Nauruan to `TitleLanguage`**:

TMDB tags some titles, overviews and images with the `fo`, `tw`, `ch`
and `na` language codes, which `GetTitleLanguage` did not recognise,
so every startup logged an unrecognised-language error for each of
them. Added the four languages to the enum and to the code-to-language,
language-to-code and display-name mappings.

`feat` (`abstractions`): **Expose the performance language on cast and crew roles**:

Added `Language` and `LanguageCode` to `ICast` and `ICrew`, and a
`Language` field on the API `Role` model. AniDB and TMDB only carry the
original-language cast and crew, so their roles report the work's
original language: TMDB from the show or movie's original language,
AniDB from the language of the main title, resolved from its
transcription with the new `GetSpokenLanguage` helper. AniList lists
the cast and crew of every dub, so its roles report the language the
person works in: for the cast the voice actor's language, for the crew
the language qualifier AniList appends to dub staff roles ("ADR
Director (English)"), which is stripped from the forwarded role name,
falling back to the anime's original language when none is appended.

- `GetTitleLanguage` now also resolves english language names, with
  the few AniList uses that the enum-name fallback could not
- Added `TryGetTitleLanguage`, a probe that does not report
  unrecognised strings, so qualifiers such as "(OP)" stay out of the log

`feat`: **Estimate the air time of episodes AniList has no schedule for**:

AniList's airing schedule gives a precise broadcast time, but only for
the episodes it has scheduled. AniDB has a date for nearly every
episode, including future ones, and already reflects breaks and delays.
The shoko episode now combines the two: when an episode has an AniDB
date but no linked AniList schedule entry, its air time is the AniDB
date, taken as midnight UTC, plus the broadcast time learned from the
series' other linked episodes.

- `AirTimeUtility.LearnAirTimeOffset` takes the median offset over the
  ten most recent aired normal episodes with a known time, so a
  long-running series follows its current slot and a one-off special
  or delay does not skew it; fewer than two samples yields nothing
- `AnimeSeries.AnilistAirTimeOffset` caches the learned offset, reset
  on link and schedule changes and self-healing after an hour
- `AnimeEpisode` applies it in `AirDateWithTime` for normal episodes and
  reports it through the new `IShokoEpisode.IsAirTimeEstimated`
- `IEpisode.AirDate` on the shoko episode is now the UTC calendar day
  of `AirDateWithTime`, so the two never disagree, and a linked series
  takes its days from AniList's broadcast schedule rather than an AniDB
  date that records an early screening
- The AniDB and AniList entities are untouched, and the episode
  matchers keep reading those entities, so estimates never feed matching

`fix` (`core`): **Keep the database blocked after a failed startup**:

`DatabaseUnblockLoop` waited on the blocking tasks with `WaitAny`, which
returns for a faulted task the same as for a completed one, so when
startup failed and the startup task was faulted the loop removed it,
found nothing else blocking, and lifted the block. `IsDatabaseBlocked`
turned false, the `[DatabaseRequired]` acquisition filter let every job
through, and `WaitForDatabaseUnblockedAsync` resolved successfully, all
against repositories that were never loaded. A plugin's recurring sweep
job hit a `NullReferenceException` in `BaseCachedRepository` eight times
this way.

A faulted or cancelled blocking task now keeps the block up and fails
the waiters with the same exception instead.

`fix` (`core`): **Halt the queue for good when startup fails**:

The queue's hosted services are up before the database is, so after a
failed startup the orchestrator kept dispatching whatever the acquisition
filters let through, and a client could resume it through the API or
SignalR at any time. Nothing in a failed process can serve a job.

- Added `Halt` to the orchestrator and `IQueueScheduler`: a pause that
  `Resume` cannot undo for the rest of the process lifetime, with
  `IsHalted` alongside `IsPaused`
- `WorkerPoolManager.Resume` no longer announces a start on a halted queue
- `SystemService` halts the queue when `StartupFailedException` is set

`feat` (`api`): **Put the broadcast time and filters on the calendar episodes**:

`Dashboard.Episode` took its air date straight from the AniDB episode,
so the calendar never saw the times AniList provides or the estimates
the shoko episode derives from them. It now reads the shoko episode
when there is one.

- `AirDate` is the shoko episode's day, the UTC calendar day of the
  broadcast when the time is known
- Added `AiredAt`, the UTC air time, set to midnight on `AirDate` when
  no time is known, with `HasAirTime` and `IsAirTimeEstimated` flags so
  a client can tell a real time from the placeholder
- `CalendarEpisodes` fetches a day either side of the requested range
  and filters on the final day, since a late-night slot can move an
  episode across midnight UTC, and orders by the air time
- Added `includeWithAirTime`, an `IncludeOnlyFilter` on the known
  broadcast time, and a comma-delimited `type` filter on the AniDB
  episode type that defaults to normal episodes
- A series counts as missing when it has no files, not merely when
  Shoko has no entry for it; the series and shoko episode stay attached
  so the card keeps its link and broadcast time

- `AutoAnimeGroupCalculator` — the relation-graph walk and fuzzy title

`repo` (`workflows`): **Run the unit test suites in CI**:

`integration-tests.yml` was the only workflow invoking `dotnet test`, and it
runs `Shoko.IntegrationTests` alone. `Shoko.Tests` and
`Shoko.QueueProcessor.Tests` had never gated a merge, so either could be
broken without CI noticing.

Both suites are self-contained — no database, no network and no native
dependencies — so the job needs none of the setup the integration tests do
and finishes in seconds.

`test`: **Cover filter expression persistence and the sorting selectors**:

Two areas that had no coverage and fail quietly when they break.

**Stored filter expressions.** `FilterPreset.Expression` and
`SortingExpression` are persisted as JSON that records each node by its
*simple* class name. `SimpleNameSerializationBinder.BindToType` resolves
that name by scanning loaded assemblies and taking the first match, and
returns `null` when nothing matches — which `FilterExpressionConverter`
swallows through its error handler. So renaming or moving an expression
turns every filter using it into a broken one, with nothing raised at the
call site, and two types sharing a simple name would bind to whichever the
scan happened to find first.

Covers all 284 concrete expression types: each binds back to its own type,
no two share a simple name, and every constructible one survives a
round-trip. Also pins that a name outside the `FilterExpression` hierarchy
does not bind, which is what stops stored JSON naming arbitrary types.

**Sorting selectors.** 76 of them, previously untested. Beyond evaluating
to a non-null comparable, each is checked against the flags the filtering
engine caches on: a selector that reads user info must declare
`UserDependent`, and one whose value moves with the clock must declare
`TimeDependent`.

`FilterableFactory` populates the filterable doubles by reflection rather
than by hand, so a member added to the interface later cannot silently
arrive as null in tests that look like they cover it. `TestFilterable`'s
two image-type properties gained `init` so they can be populated like every
sibling.

`refactor` (`relocation`): **Resolve file system access through `IFileSystemHelpers`**:

`FileSystemHelpers` was a concrete class, so nothing that moves or deletes a
user's files could be exercised without a real disk. Extracted the interface
it already implicitly had and switched every consumer to it. The concrete
type stays registered and the interface resolves to the same singleton, so
behaviour is unchanged.

Added tests over the guards in `DirectlyRelocateFile`, which had none. They
run against a mocked file system, and a rejected request is proven by the
mock never being asked to move, delete or create anything:

- requests with no managed folder, no relative path, or already cancelled
- relative paths climbing out of the managed folder
- files in an excluded folder, or in a drop destination when relocating
  inside destinations is disabled
- a source file that is missing on disk

One of these pins a subtle protection: containment is a prefix comparison,
and it is only correct because `ShokoManagedFolder.Path` always ends in a
directory separator. Without it a relative path could reach a sibling folder
sharing a prefix — `/media/animeX` against `/media/anime` — and write
outside the managed folder. Both that and the separator itself are now
covered.

`test`: **Cover how video playback updates fold into stored user data**:

`UserDataService` decides whether a file counts as watched, how far through
it the user is, and how many times they have seen it — the state the whole
watched/unwatched view of a collection is built on — and none of it was

goes wrong:

  because the value alone proves nothing when the tests run on a machine set

- An update carrying no changes must not write. Playback progress reports
  arrive continuously, so a needless save there is a write per second per
  client.

`CachedRepo.BuildWritable` extends the harness to writes: a partial mock
keeps every real read path and replaces only the virtual `Save`/`Delete`,
landing them in the same cache the reads come from, so a saved entity is

`refactor` (`anidb`): **Resolve the UDP socket through a factory**:

`AniDBUDPConnectionHandler` constructed its `AniDBSocketHandler` inline, so
none of the protocol handling around the socket could be reached without
binding a port. `IAniDBSocketHandler` already existed; this adds the factory
to go with it and switches the field to the interface. The real factory
returns the same socket handler as before, so behaviour is unchanged.

`test`: **Cover the AniDB HTTP and UDP connection handlers**:

Neither connection handler was tested, and both carry the logic that keeps
the server out of an AniDB ban — which costs a user a day of metadata when
it goes wrong.

**HTTP.** A successful call returns the body and status; a response
containing the `>banned<` marker sets the ban and throws; a further call
while banned never reaches the network, because talking to AniDB while
banned is what extends the ban; `force` still gets through for the caller
that needs it; and a server error or transport failure is surfaced rather
than mistaken for a ban.

**UDP.** `Init` builds the socket and records whether it connected, and
refuses incomplete credentials. Commands go out as UTF-16 or ASCII as asked,
replies are decoded by their byte order mark and the mark is stripped. An
all-zero reply is treated as a ban — a silent socket cannot be told apart
from one, and assuming the worse is what stops the server digging deeper —
after which `Send` stops talking.

**No test opens a connection of any kind.** HTTP goes through a stub
`HttpMessageHandler` that answers from a queue, and UDP through a stub
`IAniDBSocketHandler` that replays canned payloads. Both are pointed at
`anidb.invalid` — reserved by RFC 2606 and guaranteed never to resolve — so
anything that did try to reach the network would fail loudly rather than
quietly succeed.

`test`: **Cover parsing of the AniDB anime XML**:

`HttpAnimeParser` turns AniDB's XML into the anime, title and episode
records the rest of the server is built on. It is pure — XML in, objects out

Covers the documents it must reject (no anime id, no main title), the anime
type mapping, episode counts, the restricted flag, titles with their type
and language, and the episode fields including type prefixes, double
episodes, and length in minutes becoming seconds.

Two pin AniDB quirks that are invisible until they break:

- `1970-01-01` is AniDB's "unknown date" sentinel. Taking it literally would
  file shows under 1970 and break every year filter and season grouping.
- Apostrophes arrive as backticks throughout the API and are translated back
  in titles and descriptions.

`fix` (`db`): **Compare list-valued columns by value when checking for changes**:

`StringListConverter`, `TmdbContentRatingConverter` and
`TmdbProductionCountryConverter` all return a `List<T>`, and all compared
with `x.Equals(y)`, which for a list is reference equality.

`NullSafeGet` builds a fresh list on every load, so the loaded value never
matched the stored one and NHibernate treated every mapped list column as
changed on every flush, rewriting rows that nobody had touched. The columns
affected are the AniDB title/tag lists and the TMDB content ratings and
production countries.

They now compare the string each side would be written as, so two lists are
the same exactly when they would produce the same column value.

`test`: **Make the sorting selector and converter tests actually able to fail**:

An adversarial review of the new suites found several that passed regardless
of what the production code did. Verified by mutation, before and after.

**Sorting selectors.** 74 of the 75 are a single property read, so "produces
a value", "is comparable", "is deterministic" and "ignores the time" could
never be false; and the two value assertions could not tell one property
from another, because `FilterableFactory` gave every property of the same
type the same sample. Changing a selector to return a sibling field kept all
381 cases green.

The factory now seeds each value from the property name, and the selectors
are pinned by a generated table of selector to the field it reads. Four
selectors mutated to read a sibling — plain, nested, user-scoped, and the
date-converting one — now each fail.

**Converters.** Both equality theories passed `x` as both arguments or two
nulls, so only the `ReferenceEquals` short-circuit ran and the comparison
that decides whether a row is rewritten was never reached. Replaced with
distinct-but-equal values per converter, which caught the list-comparison
bug fixed in the previous commit. Dropped the two that asserted a hardcoded
`typeof()` was not null and one that asserted nothing at all, and added
`MessagePackConverter<MediaContainer>` explicitly, since reflection never
yields an open generic and it had been excluded from every theory.

**AniDB HTTP.** `TheRequestGoesToTheConfiguredServer` only checked that the
relative URL it passed in came back, so the handler could ignore the
configured server entirely and stay green. Asserts the whole URI now.

Also: assert the actual date rather than not-null in the series stats,
tighten an over-broad `ThrowsAny`, drop a strictly weaker duplicate in the
release management tests, and correct a class comment that claimed ranking
was exercised when only redundancy is.

`test`: **Cover playlist DSL rejection, and record the broken extras syntax**:

The playlist DSL is user-supplied text from the v3 API, so how it turns bad

`test`: **Close the gaps a third review found**:

**An empty playlist entry was not really covered.** The test asserted only

**Four converters looked covered for equality but were not.** They appeared

exists to catch. Covered in both directions now, and a check asserts the two

the other.

Also corrected the diagnosis recorded for the playlist extras bug. The split

span overload and searches for the two-character sequence `"+ "`, which
never occurs. Either correction alone still fails; with both, the parser
accepts all four documented forms, which is now measured rather than
assumed.

`test`: **Assert the documented playlist extras syntax, skipped pending a fix**:

Replaces the earlier placeholder with the six examples taken from
`ParsePlaylist`'s own remarks, covering the group and series branches, and
written against the intended behaviour so it turns green when the parsing is
corrected.

The entry is split on `+` before the extras suffix is looked for, so the
suffix survives as a separate sub-item and is rejected; `recursive` is taken
for a release group ID because it begins with `r`. This has never worked —
the first version split on `+` and then searched the result for `+`, which
could never match — so nothing regressed, and two years without a report
suggests the flags are unused.

Correcting the split alone is not enough: `IndexOf(['+', ' '])` binds to the
span overload and looks for the literal sequence `"+ "`, so `IndexOfAny` is
needed too. Both were measured.

`test`: **Drop the playlist extras assertion**:

The documented `g<id>+<extra>` syntax cannot be demonstrated as a defect.
`items` arrives through `[FromQuery]`, and a query string decodes `+` to a
space, so a client following the documentation sends `g5+recursive` and the
service receives `g5 recursive`. The literal `+` only survives if the client
percent-encodes it.

That makes the suffix indistinguishable from a second sub-item once decoded,
which is why the parser accepts either delimiter, and means the syntax is
not expressible over this transport rather than being mis-parsed. The
remaining rejection tests are unaffected.

`test` (`db`): **Compare the three backend schemas column by column**:

The three backends each keep their own hand-written DDL, and nothing forced them to
agree. `SchemaParityTests` compared tables and primary keys only, so a column added,
widened or made nullable on one backend and missed on another went unnoticed —
`add missing primary keys on SQL Server for 38 tables` and
`widen TMDB_Show/TMDB_Movie Genres column on MySQL and SQL Server` were both that.

The new comparison reads the catalog of a real database of each backend rather than
replaying the DDL, because a replay cannot see the whole migration: MySQL performs some
of its through `PREPARE stmt FROM @sqlstmt`, and every backend has migrations written
in C#. Nothing is committed — a recorded schema is a copy that falls behind the
migrations it claims to describe — so the dumps are produced at runtime and compared
side by side.

- `SchemaSnapshot` reduces a backend's catalog to a type family, declared width and
  nullability per column, so the dialects can be compared at all
- `SchemaSnapshotTests` writes the dump for the backend it just migrated
- `SchemaTypeParityTests` compares the three, and skips rather than passes when they
  are not all present
- CI publishes each job's dump and adds a `schema-parity` job over all three
- `scripts/compare_schemas.sh` runs the whole thing locally against Docker

SQLite takes no part in the width comparison, having no declared widths, and its
`INTEGER` is treated as `BIGINT`, which it is.

The comparison currently fails: 6 columns differ in type, 15 in width between MySQL and
SQL Server, and 110 in nullability. It reports them in full so the list can be worked
through.

`fix` (`db`): **Hold every backend to the nullability its model declares**:

`SchemaTypeParityTests` found 110 columns whose nullability differed between the three
backends. Every one of them backs a non-nullable model property — `string MainTitle`,
`DateTime LastUpdatedAt` — so a null could never have been read back into one, and
SQLite already agreed with the model on 93 of the 95 it could be checked against.

Most of the MySQL half was one cause: `MySQLFixUTF8` and `MySQLFixUTF8MB4` rebuild every
text column with `MODIFY`, which replaces the whole column definition and silently drops
any attribute left unstated. 83 columns lost `NOT NULL` that way, `AniDB_Anime.MainTitle`
among them, despite its `CREATE TABLE` declaring it. Those two are versioned migrations
that have already run, so they are left alone and the columns are repaired instead.

- MySQL v185 tightens 90 columns
- SQL Server v183 tightens 25, mostly TMDB `CreatedAt`/`LastUpdatedAt`
- SQLite v164 tightens `AniDB_Anime_Title.Title` and `VideoLocal.DateTimeCreated`

Each fills its nulls before altering, since a stored null would fail the alter.

SQLite cannot tighten a column in place, so `MakeColumnNotNull` rebuilds the table around
a `CREATE TABLE` patched from the one the database reports. It has to come from the
database: `MoveAnidbFileDataToReleaseInfoFormat` is a `PostDatabaseFix`, which runs after
every other command, so a database migrating in one pass still has the `CRC32`, `MD5` and
`SHA1` columns that one migrating from an older version dropped long ago. Both shapes are
covered by `SqliteNotNullVariantTests`.

Verified against all three backends, migrating from empty and, for MySQL and SQL Server,
upgrading a database already at the previous version.

`fix` (`db`): **Repair the columns only damaged when the database is pre-created**:

The v185 list was derived from a database Shoko had created itself, which uses
utf8mb4_unicode_ci — so `MySQLFixUTF8MB4` had nothing to convert for six columns and they
kept their `NOT NULL`. A database created outside Shoko keeps the server's default
collation instead, and the conversion then reaches those too.

CI creates the schema through `MARIADB_DATABASE`, so it hit exactly that and reported six

`Versions.VersionValue`.

Since every text column is converted when none of them match, this is the whole of the
damage rather than another instalment of it. Verified against a database created the way
CI creates it, both migrating from empty and upgrading one already at v185.

`fix` (`db`): **Skip runtime-emitted assemblies when resolving a filter's type**:

`BindToType` scans every loaded assembly, and `GetTypes()` throws
`ReflectionTypeLoadException` on one that is still being written to. The throw reaches
`FilterExpressionConverter.ConvertFrom`, whose error handler sets `Handled` and hands back

CI hit it on six of the 287 `EveryConstructibleExpressionSurvivesARoundTrip` cases, spread
across unrelated namespaces — whichever happened to be deserializing while a Castle proxy
was being emitted for a mock elsewhere in the run.

Nothing bound here is ever emitted at runtime, so skipping dynamic assemblies costs
nothing. Reproduced by mocking distinct interfaces while scanning, which threw 32, 52 and
40 times across three runs, and threw none once the assemblies were skipped.

`SimpleNameSerializationBinderTests` reproduces the scan failing while assemblies are

`SlotsExpireAfterWindow_AllowsNewCalls` asserted that two calls finish within 200ms after

`TheScanSurvivesAssembliesBeingEmittedAlongsideIt` passed its cancellation token to

`OnEnqueue_MaxBatchReached_TriggersImmediateFlush` slept 100ms and asserted a

`fix` (`db`): **Keep the case-sensitive collation MySQL's text conversion undoes**:

v170 made twelve columns `utf8mb4_bin` so that hashes, paths and tokens
compare case-sensitively. v185 rebuilt ten of them with `MODIFY`, which
replaces the whole definition, and every one of those named
`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` — quietly making `VideoLocal.Hash`,
`VideoLocal_Place.FilePath` and `ImportFolder.ImportFolderLocation`
case-insensitive again on any database upgrading through it. Each of the
ten now restates the collation the column already has.

`MySQLFixUTF8` undid the same thing, and had been doing so since v170. It
is a `PostDatabaseFix`, so on a database migrating in one pass it runs
after every patch, and it converted anything not already
`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` — v170's columns included, dropping their `NOT NULL`
along the way. A fresh install therefore ended up case-insensitive where
one that upgraded step by step, having recorded the fix long ago, stayed
case-sensitive. It now leaves `utf8mb4_bin` alone, which is already
utf8mb4 and never what it was written to convert.

`SchemaTypeParityTests` cannot see a collation, so neither showed up
there. Verified on MariaDB migrating from empty: all twelve keep
`utf8mb4_bin`, and no column is left on any other collation.

`fix` (`db`): **Give SQLite the column types the other two backends declare**:

`SchemaTypeParityTests` found six columns SQLite stores under a different
type family than MySQL and SQL Server do:

- `AniDB_Anime.AirDate` and `EndDate` became `varchar(10)` on MySQL at
  v171 and on SQL Server at v167, when they became a `PartialDateOnly`.
  SQLite never got that migration and kept the `DATETIME` it was created
  as, so rows written before the change still carry a time of day the
  other two dropped
- `AnimeEpisode_User.UserTags` and `AnimeSeries_User.UserTags` were added
  by an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` that named no type at all, leaving
  them with BLOB affinity where the model maps a `StringListConverter`
- `TMDB_Episode.Runtime` and `TMDB_Movie.Runtime` map `RuntimeMinutes`,
  an `int?`, but were created `TEXT`

SQLite cannot retype a column in place, so v165 rebuilds each table the
way v164 does for nullability. `RetypedVariantOf` patches the type into
the table's own `CREATE TABLE`, read from the database rather than
written out here, and replaces only the type: the constraints that follow
carry the nullability, the default and the primary key. It has to cope
with a type that is several words, brackets a comma, or is not there at
all, all of which `SqliteRetypedVariantTests` covers.

Verified against all three backends migrating from empty.

`fix` (`db`): **Declare one width per column across the three backends**:

`SchemaTypeParityTests` found fifteen columns MySQL and SQL Server
declare at different widths. In every case one of the two already bounds
the column and the other leaves it unbounded, so the bound is what the
data already is — nothing longer can ever have been written on the
backend that enforces it. Each takes the bound.

- MySQL v186 narrows eight `text` columns SQL Server bounds:
  `AniDB_Anime_Relation.RelationType` to 100, `ScanFile.Hash` and
  `HashResult` to 100, `AnimeSeries.AirsOn` to 10, `FilterPreset.Name` to
  250, and three user-entered titles to 500
- SQL Server v184 narrows seven `MAX` columns MySQL bounds:
  `AniDB_Episode.Rating` and `Votes` to 200, `AnimeSeries`'s two default
  languages to 50, both `ImportFolder` columns to 500, and
  `TMDB_Person.PlaceOfBirth` to 128

Each trims its values to the width first, since anything longer would
fail the alter. `FilterPreset.Name` drops its index before the alter and
recreates it after: MySQL indexed it by a 255-character prefix, which no
longer fits a 250-character column, and a bounded column does not need
one.

Verified against all three backends, migrating from empty and, for MySQL
and SQL Server, upgrading a database seeded with values too long for the
new width — every one is trimmed rather than failing the migration.

`fix` (`release`): **Allow a release to list the same episode more than once**:

`CheckCrossReferences` inferred invalidity from a count difference, so
every deliberate collapse had to be compensated by hand. The `DistinctBy`
that merges identical percentage ranges never was, so a release listing
one episode twice threw `Release have 1 invalid cross reference(s)`
instead of saving. AniDB serves that shape whenever a file's related
episode points back at its own base episode.

- Replaced the count reconciliation with an explicit `invalidXrefs`
  count, raised only where a cross-reference is genuinely rejected — an
  episode ID that is `<= 0`, or one AniDB answers `NO_SUCH_EPISODE` for
- Normalised percentage ranges into the contract documented on
  `IReleaseVideoCrossReference` rather than rejecting them: both bounds
  are clamped before the range is reversed, so an out-of-range pair can
  no longer come back out with the start past the end, and a zero-length
  range is corrected to cover the whole episode
- Kept the narrower-range override, so a related entry still replaces the
  base entry's full range

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Drop the series memo when an episode mapping changes**:

`GetTmdbOverviews` reads the linked season and episode cross-references, so
in the season-zero case a series' overview comes from an episode mapping
rather than from the show, and changing one has to invalidate the memo.
`ResetAllEpisodeLinks`, `SetEpisodeLink` and `MatchAnidbToTmdbEpisodes` all
write those cross-references and none of them did. The last one resets after
its save, which is past the early return for a preview, so a dry run still
writes and invalidates nothing.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Drop the memoised titles when a refresh rewrites the rows**:

`AniDB_Anime`, `AniDB_Episode` and `AnimeEpisode` memoise their default title
on first read, but the rows belong to `AniDB_Anime_Title` and
`AniDB_Episode_Title`, which are served by repositories of their own, and the
entities come from cached repositories that outlive the refresh. Writing the
rows said nothing to the entity holding the memo, so a placeholder episode
title stayed until a restart even though the real one had already arrived.

- Added `ResetDefaultTitle` to the three entities, beside the field it clears.
  None of them implement `IEntityMetadata`, so the `ResetAllTitles` seam the
  TMDB entities use was not available here
- Invalidated the episodes named by the title rows that were actually written
  or removed, and the anime only when its own title rows changed, so the
  decision is made from the write itself rather than a higher-level flag

`fix` (`anidb`): **Assign the default title to its own field**:

`AniDB_Anime.DefaultTitle` wrote both of its fallback results to
`_preferredTitle`, the field behind `PreferredTitle`. That corrupted the
preferred-title memo with a default title and left `_defaultTitle` null, so
every read for an anime without a main title re-ran the whole fallback,
including the `AniDBTitleHelper` lookup. Only an anime with no
`TitleType.Main` row reaches either branch, which is presumably why it went
unnoticed. The first branch also memoised the `FirstOrDefault` result before
its null check, so that is a pattern match now.

`fix` (`shoko`): **Drop the memoised series default title when its inputs change**:

`AnimeSeries.DefaultTitle` memoises the title override, falling back to the
AniDB anime's own default title, and it was the last of the five title
accessors with no way to clear the memo. The override paths cleared the
preferred and anime titles but not this one, and the AniDB refresh cleared
`AniDB_Anime`'s memo without touching the series, which caches the result of
reading it, so a renamed series kept its old title until a restart.

- Added `ResetDefaultTitle`, matching the three AniDB entities
- Called it where an input actually changes: both override endpoints, v3 and
  v1, and the AniDB refresh where the anime's titles were rewritten
- Left the TMDB reset sites alone. The memo has no TMDB input, so clearing it
  there would imply a dependency that does not exist

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Only clear the series overview when an episode mapping changes**:

`GetTmdbTitles` reads the linked show or movie and nothing below it, while
`GetTmdbOverviews` descends into the season and episode cross-references, so
an episode mapping can only move the overview. The episode paths were clearing

imply an input they do not have.

- Added `ResetSeriesOverview` beside `ResetSeriesTitlesAndOverview` and moved

- Left the five show and movie paths as they were, since linking either one

`fix` (`images`): **Fall back to the other series in a group without images**:

main series had none — an AniDB anime without a poster, for instance —
reported no images at all even when its sibling series had art. That also
contradicted `AnimeGroup.AvailableImageTypes`, which already aggregates
across `AllSeries`.

  otherwise be left blank, so groups that already resolve an image keep
  the images and the ordering they had

  entity can be reached through more than one series and

`feat` (`api`): **Offer a source URL for images the server does not hold**:

An image the server has no local copy of could not be shown at all. The
records exist, since every image a provider reports is stored, but only the
ones inside the preferred languages and the per-entity limit are downloaded,
and `GET /api/v3/Image/{imageID}` answers 404 for the rest because the stream
is read from disk. A client had no way to reach the original, so an image
picker could only ever offer what had already been fetched.

Serving them through the server was tried before, in 5.0, and removed for
good reason: `Image_Base.GetStream` downloaded and wrote the file during the
request, blocking a thread per image. Handing out the URL instead leaves the
fetching to the client and costs the server nothing.

- Added `RemoteURL` to the `Image` and `ImageSlim` DTOs, left out of the
  payload when there is nothing to say
- Added a `includeRemoteUrl` query parameter to the endpoints that serve those
  DTOs, defaulting to `WhenUnavailable` so the field is only filled in for
  images that cannot be served from here, which makes its presence the signal
  that the client has to go elsewhere
- Gave it a `RemoteUrlInclusion` of its own rather than reusing
  `IncludeOnlyFilter`, whose `only` narrows the result set and would read as
  "return just the unavailable images"
- Built the URL from the source's registered template, so a custom mirror is
  honoured and a source without one simply reports nothing
- Documented the new parameter, filled in the `<param>` tags that were empty
  on the image endpoints, and wrote doc comments for the TMDB image endpoints,
  which had none

Nothing changes for a caller that does not ask: images nested in the series,
group, role and playlist DTOs carry no URL, and `includeUndesired` still
defaults to `false`, so a picker has to opt in to see undownloaded images.

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Drop the memoised titles and overviews when they are written**:

The TMDB entities memoise their titles and overviews on first read, but the
rows themselves belong to `TMDB_Title` and `TMDB_Overview`, which are served by
direct repositories. Writing to those said nothing to the entity holding the
memoised copy, and the entities come from cached repositories that outlive any
one request, so a title corrected on TMDB stayed stale for the life of the
process — a forced refresh reported no change, and only a restart brought the
new value through.

`AnimeSeries` compounded it. `ResetAnimeTitles` and `ResetPreferredOverview`
run right after a TMDB refresh and rebuild by reading back through the entity,
so they re-cached the stale values as fresh. `ResetPreferredTitle` never
cleared anything at all: its guard returned early precisely when a title was
cached, making every one of its call sites a no-op.

- Added `ResetAllTitles` and `ResetAllOverviews` to `IEntityMetadata`, with
  default empty bodies so an entity overrides only what it actually memoises,
  and implemented them on `TMDB_Movie`, `TMDB_Show`, `TMDB_Season`,
  `TMDB_Episode`, `TMDB_Collection` and `TMDB_Person`
- Dropped the memoised copies in `UpdateTitlesAndOverviewsWithTuple` as soon as
  the rows are saved, so the series-level resets that follow rebuild from the
  new values rather than the old ones
- Fixed `ResetPreferredTitle` to clear unconditionally, matching
  `ResetPreferredOverview` and `AniDB_Anime.ResetPreferredTitle`. It stays
  eager because `AnimeSeriesRepository.RegenerateDb` uses it to warm the cache
  on startup

The purge paths need no invalidation of their own: they delete the entity from
its cached repository, so the memoised copy goes with it.

Closes #1422

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Store the biographies fetched for a staff member**:

`UpdatePerson` asked TMDB for `PersonMethods.Translations` and then only ran
`Populate`, which keeps the English biography and drops the rest. Nothing else
wrote a `TMDB_Overview` row for a person, so `GetAllBiographies` always came
back empty and `GetPreferredBiography` always fell through to the English
fallback, whatever the preferred description languages were set to.

- Reconciled the biographies from the translations already on hand, so they are
  stored the way every other entity's overviews are
- Added an `includeTitles` flag to `UpdateTitlesAndOverviews`, passed as
  `false` here. A person has no titles to speak of — you would not translate a
  given name or a family name — so TMDB carries none and `TMDB_Person` has
  nothing to read them back with; without the flag the English name would be
  written as a title row that nothing ever reads
- Purged the biographies in `PurgePersonInternal`, which removed the person,
  their images and their cast and crew roles but left their overviews behind.
  That was harmless while nothing wrote them and an orphaned row once
  something did

`refactor` (`anidb`): **Skip MyList sync steps that would write nothing**:

A sync planned and queued a removal for every entry the library no longer
had, without checking whether the entry was already at the state the delete
type marks with. Under `MarkDeleted` such an entry stays in the MyList and
keeps reading as missing, so every sync re-queued the same no-op edit against
it — thousands per run on a large list, each one taking a turn in the
`AniDB_UDP` concurrency group ahead of real work. The same hole existed on the
watched path, where a decided update that `IsInDesiredState` disagreed with
was enqueued anyway.

- Skipped the enqueue in `SyncInternalAsync` when the entry already holds the
  marked state, on both the file and the generic episode paths, and did the
  same in `ReconcileEntry`
- Renamed `MylistSyncActionKind.AlreadyInDesiredState` to `NoOperation`, which
  no longer implies a fault; the decision-versus-desired-state disagreement it
  used to stand for is now a warning in the log
- Added `MylistSyncOptions.IncludeNoOperations`, off by default, so a plan can
  list what a sync looked at and left alone as well as what it will do. Like
  `PlanOnly` it describes the call rather than the server, so no setting backs
  it
- Collected the plan through a `MylistSyncActionLog`, so what a no-op means for
  the plan is decided once rather than at each of the dozen sites that record
  one
- Added `EntriesAlreadyDisposed`, `EpisodesAlreadyDisposed` and `NoOperations`
  to `MylistSyncResult`, and a left-alone count to the sync summary log, so the
  removal counts dropping to zero is explained rather than just observed
- Dropped the empty-`Hash` filter in `AddMissingFiles`; a `VideoLocal` always
  has one
